editorial.headline: Used Vehicle Wholesale Is Nationally Open—But Not for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans wholesale used vehicles from passenger cars to specialist transport, open nationally across every business scale but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Used-vehicle wholesale is broader than a forecourt of pre-owned passenger cars. It covers the wholesale trade of used cars, including specialist vehicles such as ambulances, caravans, minibuses and fire engines, as well as trucks, trailers, semi-trailers, goods vehicles and other motorised transport vehicles. The defining idea is wholesale trade: moving used vehicles through the commercial supply chain rather than presenting a retail-facing activity.

The activity is open to Micro, Small, Medium and Large businesses. That breadth matters because the record does not confine the trade to a particular operating scale or vehicle category. A business may therefore organise itself around used passenger cars, commercial fleets, specialist vehicles, or a mixed vehicle portfolio, provided its activity remains within the stated wholesale scope.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clear: the activity is open to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The record cites Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 for that national position. In other words, the national framework permits full foreign ownership for a company registered to carry out this wholesale activity. That national openness, however, is not the end of the practical analysis for an investor whose intended place of registration is Bali.

In Bali, a foreign investor cannot register this activity through PMA today. The Bali assessment marks it as blocked because, at the Large scale, the OSS risk classification across every included scope is Low or Medium-Low. Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities from PMA registration across the island, on a permanent basis; the recorded trigger is the moratorium of May 2026. The result is a direct geographical constraint: national permission for up to 100% foreign ownership does not create a PMA registration route for this activity in Bali. For founders, the useful reading is straightforward—understand the wholesale scope first, then treat the Bali restriction as decisive when the proposed PMA registration is on the island.
editorial.pullQuote: National permission for up to 100% foreign ownership does not create a PMA registration route for this activity in Bali.
